ei.title: Chapter 4-12 Analysis: The Life-Saving Power of Hearing
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Vision is our dominant sense, and you want to look both ways before crossing the street — it’s the first thing parents drill into their children. But that doesn’t mean our sense of hearing isn’t a big deal. I don’t have to mention the worn-out example of cavemen and hidden saber-toothed tigers. There’s something that can sneak up and kill you today: a silent electric car. These pose an unanticipated but serious threat to pedestrians and bicyclists, who depend on engine noise to detect and orient to cars — so much so that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration now requires slow-moving electric vehicles to generate a warning noise. It’s a reminder that even for us in a modern city, having both cues can mean the difference between life and death.

det.korean: 조용한 전기차는 보행자와 자전거 이용자에게 예상치 못한 심각한 위협(an unanticipated but serious threat)을 제기한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① an unanticipated but serious threat — 예상치 못한 심각한 위협 ←정답
❌ ② a welcome alternative to gasoline engines — 환영받는 대안 (위협 맥락과 반대)
❌ ③ a reliable source of urban transportation — 신뢰할 만한 도시 교통수단 (위협을 설명하는 맥락과 무관)
❌ ④ a temporary inconvenience for drivers — 운전자의 일시적 불편 (보행자 위협 맥락과 다름)
det.tip: unanticipated = 예상치 못한, pose a threat = 위협을 제기하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
